rejected_rule.statement: The husband has extensive rights over community property, but the court retains the power to appoint a guardian or manager if necessary.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: "In ordinary circumstances, the husband is entitled to the management of it, Just as in ordinary circumstances he is entitled to the care of the person of his wife. The Court will take these rights into account just as in cases of habeas corpus relating to custody of children it will take into account the natural rights of parents. But it is always entitled, where the circumstances warrant it, to appoint some person, other than the husband, as guardian of the person or as manager of the estate of a lunatic wife."
